label: Wrong preposition after a verb, adjective, or noun
selfCheck: Check whether the word before the preposition normally requires a fixed preposition, such as interested in, responsible for, or depend on.
definition: The preposition is incompatible with the governing verb/adjective/noun or intended relation.

label: Wrong singular or plural noun form
selfCheck: Check whether the noun should be singular or plural based on its quantity, determiner, and intended meaning.
definition: Noun number conflicts with quantity, determiner, or intended reference.

label: Unnecessary tense shift in a past narrative
selfCheck: When describing one past sequence, keep the main verbs in a consistent past-time frame unless the time genuinely changes.
definition: Unmotivated switching between past and present while narrating past events.

label: Missing a, an, or the
searchLabel: article use: a, an and the
selfCheck: Check every singular countable noun: it normally needs a/an, the, or another determiner.
definition: A singular count noun or definite noun phrase lacks a/an/the.

label: Wrong noun form in a compound noun
selfCheck: Check whether the first noun is acting as a modifier; English noun modifiers are usually singular, such as data analysis or shoe shop.
definition: The first noun in a compound or attributive noun phrase has the wrong number/form.

label: Run-on sentence or comma splice
selfCheck: Check whether both sides could be complete sentences; join them with a full stop, semicolon, or a comma plus a conjunction.
definition: Independent clauses are joined only by a comma or without a boundary.

label: Unnecessary a, an, or the
searchLabel: article use: a, an, the and zero article
selfCheck: Check whether the noun is a generic plural, an uncountable noun, a proper noun, or part of a fixed expression that takes no article.
definition: An article is used with a generic plural, mass noun, proper noun, or fixed expression that takes zero article.

label: Missing -s after he, she, it, or a singular noun
selfCheck: In the present simple, add -s/-es when the subject is he, she, it, or one singular noun.
definition: A singular third-person present-tense subject takes a base verb instead of the -s form.

label: Subject–verb agreement: singular/plural mismatch
selfCheck: Find the grammatical head of the subject, then make the finite verb singular or plural to match it.
definition: Singular/plural subject and finite verb do not agree, including compound subjects.

label: Non-parallel verb forms
selfCheck: Verbs joined in the same list or structure should normally use matching forms.
definition: Coordinated verbs or complements use mismatched forms.

label: Missing be or another auxiliary verb
searchLabel: auxiliary verbs and the verb be
selfCheck: Check whether the predicate needs am/is/are/was/were, do, have, or another helping verb.
definition: A clause lacks required be/do/have or another auxiliary.

label: Countable or uncountable noun error
selfCheck: Check whether the noun can be counted in this meaning and whether it can take a plural, a/an, much, or many.
definition: A mass noun is pluralised or used with an incompatible determiner; or a count noun is treated as mass.

label: Missing preposition
selfCheck: Check whether the verb, adjective, noun, or phrase requires a preposition before its complement.
definition: A required preposition is omitted.

label: Wrong form in a to-infinitive
selfCheck: After infinitive to, use the base verb; also check whether the controlling word requires to or a bare infinitive.
definition: The verb after to is not in the base form, or required to is missing/extra.

label: Wrong object or complement pattern after a verb
selfCheck: Check how many objects or complements the verb can take and whether it requires a direct object, preposition, clause, or infinitive.
definition: A verb is used with the wrong number or type of objects/complements, including an intransitive verb used transitively.

label: Sentence fragment with no finite verb
selfCheck: A complete sentence needs a finite verb that carries tense or agrees with its subject.
definition: A phrase/list/reduced clause is presented as a complete sentence without a finite predicate.

label: Incorrect that-clause or wh-clause after a verb
selfCheck: Check the clause pattern required after verbs such as know, realise, explain, ask, and understand.
definition: A reporting or cognition verb takes a malformed content clause.

label: Wrong preposition for time, place, or movement
searchLabel: prepositions of time, place and movement
selfCheck: Choose in, on, at, to, into, from, or another preposition according to the precise time, location, or direction.
definition: in/on/at/to/into etc. is wrong in a temporal or locative phrase.

label: Determiner and noun do not agree
selfCheck: Match determiners such as this/these, each/every, much/many, and one of with the correct noun number and countability.
definition: this/these, every, each, much/many, a lot of, one of, etc. conflict with noun number/countability.

label: Wrong gerund or infinitive after a word
selfCheck: Check the pattern required by the controlling verb or adjective: verb-ing, to + base verb, or a bare infinitive.
definition: A controlling verb/adjective requires a gerund or infinitive but the wrong complement form is used.

label: Wrong choice of a, an, the, or no article
searchLabel: article use: a, an, the and zero article
selfCheck: Decide whether the noun is first-mentioned, one of many, already known, unique, generic, uncountable, or a proper noun.
definition: a/an/the/zero article is selected incorrectly.

label: Incorrect tense sequence between clauses
selfCheck: Compare the times of the linked clauses and make the tense relationship logically consistent.
definition: Reported thought/speech or linked clauses use incompatible tense sequencing.

label: Unnecessary preposition
selfCheck: Check whether the verb takes a direct object without a preposition or whether the expression normally uses no preposition.
definition: A preposition is inserted where the construction takes a direct object or zero preposition.

label: Incorrect possessive form
selfCheck: Check whether possession needs apostrophe-s, a possessive pronoun, or an of-phrase.
definition: Apostrophe-s, possessive pronoun, or of-genitive is formed incorrectly.

label: Two sentence patterns mixed together
selfCheck: Identify the two competing structures and rewrite the sentence using only one complete grammatical pattern.
definition: Two alternative clause patterns are blended into one ungrammatical construction.

label: Incorrect passive-voice form
selfCheck: Passive voice normally uses the correct form of be plus a past participle.
definition: Passive meaning lacks be + past participle or uses the wrong participle/preposition.

label: Incorrect past participle form
selfCheck: After have or in a passive construction, use the correct past participle, such as written, chosen, or broken.
definition: Wrong participle after have/be or in a reduced passive construction.

label: Incorrect relative-clause structure
selfCheck: After who/which/that, do not add an extra subject or object when the relative word already fills that role.
definition: The relative clause has an extra/missing subject, resumptive pronoun, or incompatible structure.

label: Dependent-clause fragment
selfCheck: A clause beginning with because, although, if, when, or another subordinator usually needs a main clause.
definition: A subordinated because/if/although/when clause is punctuated as a complete sentence.

label: Non-parallel list or paired structure
selfCheck: Make items in a list or paired construction use the same grammatical form and function.
definition: Items in a list/correlative construction have inconsistent grammatical forms.

label: Incorrect present or past perfect
selfCheck: Use have/has/had + past participle only when the event's relationship to another time requires the perfect aspect.
definition: Present/past perfect is used incorrectly or omitted where the temporal relation requires it.

label: Incorrect question word order
selfCheck: Direct questions usually invert the subject and auxiliary; embedded questions use statement word order.
definition: Direct question lacks subject–auxiliary inversion or required auxiliary.

label: Wrong verb form after a preposition
selfCheck: A verb following a preposition normally takes the -ing form.
definition: A preposition is followed by a finite/base verb instead of a gerund/noun phrase.

label: Wrong word form or part of speech
searchLabel: word forms and parts of speech
selfCheck: Check whether this position requires a noun, verb, adjective or adverb, and use the correct derived form of the word.
definition: A related word is used in the wrong grammatical category or derived form, such as a noun where a verb is required or an adjective where a noun is required.

label: Incorrect adjective complement or predicate
selfCheck: Check whether the adjective fits the subject and whether it needs be, a preposition, or a following clause/infinitive.
definition: Adjective is used with an unsuitable subject or missing complement/copula.

label: Missing or wrong conjunction
selfCheck: Choose a conjunction that expresses the intended relationship and makes the linked clauses or phrases structurally complete.
definition: Clauses or phrases are linked with an absent or unsuitable conjunction.

label: Unnecessary or incompatible determiner
selfCheck: Remove a determiner when another determiner already fills the slot or when the noun phrase does not allow it.
definition: A determiner is redundant or incompatible with the noun phrase.

label: Missing determiner before a noun
selfCheck: Check whether the noun needs my/your, this/that, some, each, another, or another determiner.
definition: A noun phrase requires a possessive, demonstrative, quantifier, or article-like determiner.

label: Wrong pronoun form: I/me/my/mine, etc.
selfCheck: Choose the pronoun form according to its job as subject, object, possessive, or reflexive.
definition: Subject/object/possessive/reflexive pronoun form is wrong.

label: Missing pronoun or required subject/object
selfCheck: Check whether every finite clause has a subject and whether the verb or preposition requires an object.
definition: A required subject, object, or possessive pronoun is omitted.

label: Adjective used instead of an adverb, or the reverse
selfCheck: Use an adjective to describe a noun or subject complement and an adverb to modify a verb, adjective, or other adverb.
definition: An adjective is used for an adverbial function or vice versa.

label: Confusion between -ed and -ing adjectives
selfCheck: Use -ing for the thing that causes a feeling and -ed for the person or thing experiencing it.
definition: Participial adjective has the wrong active/passive meaning.

label: Unclear or illogical pronoun reference
selfCheck: Make sure the pronoun points clearly to one logical noun and cannot be misread.
definition: Pronoun does not clearly or logically refer to an antecedent.

label: Incorrect comparative or superlative form
selfCheck: Use the correct -er/-est or more/most form and the correct than or as...as structure.
definition: Comparative/superlative morphology or than/as structure is incorrect.

label: Dangling or misattached modifier
selfCheck: The noun immediately after an introductory modifier should be the person or thing performing that modifier's action.
definition: An introductory or participial modifier attaches to the wrong grammatical subject.

label: Clause needs a finite verb
selfCheck: A main clause needs a verb marked for tense or modality, not only an -ing or participle phrase.
definition: A gerund/participle phrase is used where the clause needs a finite verb.

label: Incorrect noun-phrase structure
selfCheck: Identify the head noun, then arrange determiners, possessives, adjectives, and noun modifiers around it without duplication.
definition: The internal structure of a noun phrase is fused, redundant or arranged in a non-grammatical pattern.

label: Unnecessary be or another auxiliary verb
selfCheck: Check whether an extra helping verb has created two competing finite verb forms.
definition: An extra be/do/have produces a double-verb or malformed predicate.

label: Double linker: because...so or although...but
selfCheck: Use one linker for the relationship: because without so, or although/even though without but.
definition: Because...so, although...but, even though...but, etc. redundantly mark the same relation.

label: Incorrect modal-verb construction
selfCheck: After a modal such as can, could, must, should, or may, use the base verb without to or -s.
definition: Modal meaning/form is incorrect, including mustn't scare, can not caught, etc.

label: Wrong or missing relative pronoun
selfCheck: Choose the relative word according to the antecedent and its role inside the relative clause.
definition: who/which/that/where/what is missing or incorrectly selected.

label: Verb tense conflicts with the time expression
selfCheck: Match the verb tense to explicit time words and the actual timing of the event.
definition: Verb tense does not match an explicit time expression or temporal context.

label: Incorrect it/there sentence pattern
selfCheck: Check whether the sentence needs existential there, anticipatory it, or an ordinary referential subject.
definition: Extraposition, existential there, or anticipatory it is malformed.

label: Incorrect simple-past verb form
selfCheck: Use the standard past form, especially for irregular verbs such as fell, broke, wrote, and chose.
definition: Wrong or non-standard simple-past morphology.

label: Unnecessary -s on a present-tense verb
selfCheck: Do not add -s when the present-simple subject is I, you, we, they, or plural.
definition: A plural/non-third-person subject is followed by an -s verb.

label: Incorrect tense in an if/when future condition
selfCheck: Match the tense and modal forms to the intended real, hypothetical, or past-unreal condition.
definition: Tense or modal in an if/when clause does not match the intended conditional/future meaning.

label: Wrong verb form after make, let, or help
searchLabel: make, let and help verb patterns
selfCheck: Make and let normally take object + base verb; help can take object + base verb or to-infinitive.
definition: Make, let or help is followed by an incorrect object/complement or non-base verb form.

label: Incorrect clause after be, seem, think, or a similar expression
selfCheck: Check whether the expression requires that, whether/if, a wh-clause, an infinitive, or a noun phrase.
definition: A clause functioning after a copular or reporting expression is missing or misforms its required complement structure.

label: Wrong verb form after a modal or auxiliary
searchLabel: verb forms after auxiliaries and modals
selfCheck: Use the base form after do or a modal, the past participle after have, and the required participle/complement after be.
definition: A modal, do-support, or auxiliary is followed by an inflected form instead of the base/participle form required.

label: Incorrect English word order
selfCheck: Arrange the subject, verb, object, complements, and adverbs in standard English order for this clause type.
definition: Adverbs, objects, complements, or question elements are in non-English order.

label: Unnecessary pronoun or double subject/object
selfCheck: Remove the pronoun when the noun phrase already fills the same subject or object role.
definition: A redundant pronoun creates a double subject/object.

label: Incorrect appositive phrase structure
selfCheck: An appositive must rename a nearby noun and attach clearly to it without replacing a required clause element.
definition: An appositive noun phrase is attached without a valid grammatical relationship to the clause it explains.

label: Incorrect coordination with and, or, or but
searchLabel: coordination with and, or and but
selfCheck: Make the coordinated elements grammatically compatible and ensure shared words apply logically to each item.
definition: Coordinated elements do not share compatible grammatical structure or scope.

label: Pronoun does not agree with its antecedent
selfCheck: Match the pronoun's number and person to the noun it refers to.
definition: Pronoun number/person does not agree with its antecedent.

label: There is/are agreement error
selfCheck: Match is/are or was/were to the following notional subject in a there-construction.
definition: The verb in a there is/are construction does not agree with the notional subject.

label: Incorrect if-clause and result-clause structure
selfCheck: Make sure the condition and result form one complete logical conditional pattern.
definition: If-clause and result clause are structurally or semantically mismatched.

label: Incorrect negative sentence form
selfCheck: Place not correctly and use do-support or the appropriate auxiliary when the main verb cannot carry negation directly.
definition: Negative placement, do-support, or negative polarity is malformed.
